Article.ArticleTitle: Efficacy and Renal Safety of SGLT2 Inhibitors in Type 2 Diabetes: A Randomized Controlled Trial

Abstract.AbstractText: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors reduce cardiovascular events in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
We conducted a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving 1,200 adult patients with type 2 diabetes and mild chronic kidney disease.

SGLT2 inhibition significantly slowed the decline of estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) by 1.8 mL/min/1.73 m2 per year compared to placebo (p < 0.001). Adverse events including ketoacidosis were rare but observed in 0.4% of participants.
In adults with type 2 diabetes and mild renal impairment, SGLT2 inhibitors provide renal preservation and glycemic improvement without excess serious adverse events.

Article.ArticleTitle: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists versus SGLT2 Inhibitors for Heart Failure Outcomes

Abstract.AbstractText: Both GLP-1 receptor agonists and SGLT2 inhibitors improve glycemic control, but comparative cardiovascular outcomes remain an area of clinical inquiry.

SGLT2 inhibitors exhibited a 28% reduction in hospitalization for heart failure compared with GLP-1 receptor agonists (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.61-0.85). Conversely, GLP-1 receptor agonists showed greater total weight reduction.
For heart failure risk reduction, SGLT2 inhibitors demonstrate superior protection compared to GLP-1 receptor agonists in diabetic cohorts.
